chapter: Lu Barker and the Barbarin family
title: House of the Rising Sun at the Superdome and Lu's talent
summary: Lu learned The House of the Rising Sun in an afternoon but sang Basin Street Blues, concluding her talent was for outside the church.

story.theme_name: Church, faith and religion in a musician's life
story.community_name: Church, faith and jazz: the sacred and the secular

blocks.x: So after that, maybe it was about two years ago, that they wanted us to go to the Superdome. And this guy wrote and asked me, did I know "The House Of The Rising Sun." Well, I had never heard "The House Of The Rising Sun." I didn't know nothing about it. So I asked Danny, I said, "Do you know anything about 'The House Of The Rising Sun?'" So he said, "Yeah. I've got a record back there with it." I said, "You have?" He said, "Yes." So I said, "Lord, that's a whole lot... I can't learn no new records," but I said, "Give me the record." So he gave me the record. And he was going somewhere. So I came in and then I got the paper and pencil, and I started writing "The House Of The Rising Sun." So by the time he comes back, I say, "I got it. I've got my version of it, but I know it." So I said, "Well, I'll sing it."

So then we went to the Superdome to meet the man, and I sang. And they were going to demonstrate some boats, and so I would sing this song in New Orleans with the boats. And then I sang "Basin Street Blues." So him and Danny decided that for what they were doing, instead of singing "The House Of The Rising Sun," because it's suggestive, it's about a sporting house woman, I sing the "Basin Street Blues," and that would be better. So that night, instead of singing "The House Of The Rising Sun," I sang "Basin Street Blues." So I decided right there... Now, I couldn't learn that hymn, but I could learn that...

That sporting house song. So it wasn't for me to be in that choir. See? So when they come to ask me, I said, "I ain't supposed to be in that choir." I said, "You can't be singing the Blues and be in the choir, too." So I said, "Don't ask me any more." All I'm going to be is a benchman in the church. So that's what I am, a benchman in the church now. Because that gave me my answer.
Sure. Because if you seriously do it...
Because I couldn't read and I couldn't learn the hymns, but I could learn this so quick.
They say God gives you talent for different things. And in the church, I'm afraid to open my mouth because I'm going to say the wrong words or something. So my talent for outside, you know.
That's beautiful. I understand. I can see that.
